intro: The vocabulary of history books: inventions, models, races and the centuries, with a short look at the story of the bicycle.
b1.texto:
**Time.** **El siglo** is written in Roman numerals and read as a cardinal number: **el siglo XV** is el siglo quince. **A principios de**, **a mediados de**, **a finales de** siglo. **La época**, **la era**, **la Edad Media**, **la Edad Moderna**. **Antes de Cristo** (a. C.) and **después de Cristo** (d. C.).

**Inventions.** **Un inventor** creates **un invento**. **Inventar**, **descubrir**, **fabricar**, **mejorar**, **patentar**.

**Making things.** **Aparece** un modelo nuevo. **La fábrica** **fabrica** miles de unidades, **mejora** el diseño y vende a **los ciclistas**. A fashion **se extiende** por todo el país. Eventually, someone **organiza una carrera**.

**The tenses of history.** The indefinido tells the events: **apareció**, **duró**, **se extendió**. The imperfect describes the background: **era**, **había**, **tenía**. The historical present makes them vivid: en 1885 aparece la bicicleta moderna. And the passive is common: **fue inventada**, **fue fabricado**.

**The bicycle in one paragraph.** The first machine with two wheels and no pedals dates from 1817. Around 1860 pedals were fitted to the front wheel, and later came the high-wheel model. The modern bicycle, with a chain and two wheels of equal size, became common around 1885, and air tyres arrived in 1888. Since then it has been a way to travel, a sport and a hobby.
b2.f0: The first bicycle appeared in 1817, when a German inventor built a wooden machine with two wheels and no pedals.
b2.f1: What some took for a mere toy lasted almost fifty years as a fashion and changed how entire families got around.
b2.f2: Later, pedals were added to the front wheel, and the high-wheel model became famous across Europe.
b2.f3: The modern bicycle was mass-produced around 1885; it had a chain and two wheels of the same size.
b2.f4: With the arrival of air tyres, in 1888, journeys became much more comfortable.
b2.f5: During the twentieth century brakes and gears were improved, but the basic design remains almost the same.
b2.f6: More than a century later, the bicycle remains present in cities, in sport and in the holidays of many families.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, how many wheels did the first bicycle have?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Una máquina de madera con dos ruedas.
b4.o1.refuerzo: That would be a tricycle, not mentioned.
b5.pregunta: What does the text say about the basic design today?
b5.o0.refuerzo: El diseño básico sigue siendo casi el mismo.
b5.o1.refuerzo: The high-wheel model was only an earlier fashion.
b5.o2.refuerzo: The text says the bicycle is still present.
b6.pregunta: How is el siglo XVIII read?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Centuries are read as cardinal numbers.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Ordinals are only usual up to ten.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Indefinido: one event in the past.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The imperfect describes background, not a single event.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That is the future; the event is in the past.
b8.pregunta: Complete: the bicycle was made in a small factory.
b8.o0.refuerzo: The participle agrees with la bicicleta.
b8.o1.refuerzo: It must agree with la bicicleta: feminine.
b9.o0: The inventor improved the model without help.
b9.o0.explicacion: Mejoró sin ayuda means improved without help.
b9.o1: The inventor sold the model without help.
b9.o2: The inventor repeated the model without help.
b10.traduccion: In the middle of the nineteenth century pedals appeared.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a short history of an everyday invention for a Spanish reader.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud which invention you could not live without, and why.
